checks_performed: 1. Read full test/support/simulation/runner.ex and the diff (8734146c^ ffc31ca1). The :audit_event clause now takes `produces` (was `_produces`) and runs resource_id/resource_type through resolve_optional_ref/3 before building query_params, inside a `with` -- shape now matches task_assigned's resolve_ref/fetch_prefix pattern and instance_state's, both structurally and in ordering (prefix, then refs, then the read).

2. resolve_optional_ref/3 mirrors resolve_ref/3 exactly except the :error branch on Map.fetch returns {:ok, nil} instead of {:error, {:missing_arg, key}}. Confirmed this is the correct distinction: Audit.list_entries/1's query_params already passes resource_id/resource_type straight through and (per the pre-existing, unchanged clause body) a nil in either field is a real 'do not filter on this field' value the query context already handles -- unlike task_ref/instance_ref, which are required identifiers with no meaningful nil case. args still requires "event_type" and "prefix" (Map.fetch! / fetch_prefix), which is right since those two are never optional.

3. Fail-closed confirmed: the `with` has a single `else` clause matching {:error, reason} -> %{expected_outcome: expected, outcome: :fail, observed: {:error, reason}}, identical in shape to task_assigned's and instance_state's own else clauses. An unresolved {{produces.X}} in resource_id/resource_type now produces :fail with the resolution error, not a literal template string reaching the query.

4. Diff scope confirmed via `git diff 8734146c^ ffc31ca1 -- test/support/simulation/runner.ex`: exactly the :audit_event clause body and the new resolve_optional_ref/3 helper (inserted next to resolve_ref/3) changed. `git diff --stat` on test/support/simulation/seed.ex is empty -- untouched. No other function in runner.ex changed.

5. Read the two new tests in the 'audit_event verification method' describe block of test/letflow/simulation/runner_template_and_outcomes_test.exs: (a) 'resolves a {{produces.X}} resource_id reference and scopes the real query by it' -- dispatches a real POST /api/v1/instances HTTP step via Letflow.Router.call/2, captures the runtime-only instance_id, references it as "{{produces.instance.instance_id}}" in the audit_event outcome's resource_id, asserts :pass and that the matched real Postgres AuditEntry.resource_id equals the captured runtime id -- not hardcoded. (b) the mismatch pair using a resolved-but-wrong Ecto.UUID.generate() value, asserting :fail with matching_entry: nil even though a real row for the right event_type/resource_type exists -- proves the substitution genuinely scopes the query rather than being a no-op. Both mirror the existing task_assigned match/mismatch pattern in shape and the pre-existing audit_event match/mismatch tests (which still pass unmodified, since they don't set resource_id at all and hit resolve_optional_ref's {:ok, nil} branch).
